title: Rolling Stones Sacred Of Being Banned From U.S. Tour By Trump For Voicing Displeasure With Use Of Their Song In 'Melania' Doc - NewsBreak
text:
By Baila Eve Zisman ,
13 hours ago The Rolling Stones may face consequences for their outspoken criticism of President Donald Trump .
First Lady Melania Trump ‘s self-titled documentary, released Jan. 30, follows the First Lady-elect in the 20 days leading up to Trump’s second inauguration, and features The Rolling Stones’ song “Gimme Shelter” in an early sequence.
In the past, when Trump has used their music, The Rolling Stones have sent cease-and-desist letters and threatened legal action. However, according to an insider, the band has a new “fear” that Trump will impose repercussions for their criticism.
According to representatives for the group, the licensing of “Gimme Shelter” was given through The Rolling Stones’ home label ABKCO, and the band members had “no direct involvement.”
An inside source told AOL , “There is a growing belief that this dispute has taken a sinister turn. The fear being voiced is that Trump could look at ways to hit back, including targeting the band’s ability to tour in the U.S. by raising issues around past drug histories and visa eligibility. It really is a sinister turn in this dispute.”
Another insider reported, “For a band like the Stones, the States is a critical market, so anything that interferes with that would be hugely damaging. That’s why people close to them are taking this seriously – it’s not just a war of words, there’s a concern about tangible consequences for the group’s touring future.”

The Rolling Stones previously sent Trump a cease-and-desist letter after he played their song “You Can’t Always Get What You Want” at the 2016 Republican National Convention. They additionally posted to X that they “do not endorse Donald Trump.”
A representative for the band told Billboard in 2016, “The Rolling Stones have never given permission to the Trump campaign to use their songs. [The band] has requested that they cease all use immediately.”
Trump tried to use the song again in 2020, pushing the band to threaten legal action.
Melania producer Marc Beckman claimed that the band members “were just like, ‘Oh, you’re making a nice movie,’” when asked for their permission to use “Gimme Shelter” in the film.
However, another source close to the band claims they were not “impressed” with the documentary and have “made that known in private, and that has not gone down well.”
